Rachel — thanks for the clear summary and the attachments. Looping in Monica (CS lead) and Karthik/Soojin from infra and network eng so we have the right people on the thread.

Quick replies to your bullets below and a proposed agenda for the working session:  

- VPC peering vs private endpoints: both are viable. For multi-AZ resilience we typically recommend private endpoints + regional failover; peering is simpler for some orgs but requires CIDR non-overlap and more routing ops.
- Ports & egress: we'll capture a baseline (API ports, health checks, SSH for on-prem appliance if chosen).
- On-prem appliance: we'll share the hardware/VM sizing; the package requires outbound TLS to the control plane and a limited set of inbound management ports.
- KMS/HSM: we support bring-your-own KMS integrations; HSM options require a short integration checklist.
- Logging: syslog + optional S3/Splunk export patterns supported; retention configurable per-customer.

Proposed working session agenda (30–45m):
1) Confirm IP/CIDR constraints and preferred connectivity (peering vs private endpoints)
2) Hardware/VM sizing and access model for the appliance option
3) Auth/KMS pattern and cert rotation windows
4) Cutover timeline and blackout/maintenance windows
5) Action items and owners

Available times (PDT): Wed 5/22 10:00–11:30 or Thu 5/23 14:00–16:00. If those don't work, propose alternatives. I'm attaching our private-deploy template (redwood_private-deploy-template_v2.xlsx) so we can pre-fill details before the call.

—Vivek

Hi Rachel — quick note from the CS/ops perspective so we can start collecting the right artifacts before the meeting. If you can populate the attached template (or paste answers inline) that will speed things up for your network/security reviewers. Key items we need:  

- Public and private CIDR blocks you control (for peering) and any existing reserved ranges we should avoid
- Expected RPS/throughput for inference traffic and peak concurrent sessions (helps sizing connection pools and appliance resources)
- Egress policy: do you route to the internet via NAT gateway or through a transit gateway? Any special firewall/NGFW appliances in path?
- TLS termination: where will it happen (customer edge vs Redwood private endpoint)? If customer handles TLS, we'll provide cert rotation guidance.
- Staging environment expectations and smoke-test checklist (we prefer a 2-week staging window prior to cutover)

Hi all — thanks for the prompt responses. Quick answers from our infra team (see inline):  

- CIDR: We can provide two /16 ranges for peering in us-west-2 (10.40.0.0/16, 10.41.0.0/16). No overlap with current ranges.
- Throughput: Baseline expected egress ~600 Mbps, peak 1.8 Gbps during heavy batch jobs. Concurrent sessions ~120–150.
- Egress: We use a transit gateway and an NGFW (Palo Alto) for outbound filtering. NAT is used for internet-bound traffic.
- TLS: We prefer Redwood to terminate TLS at a private endpoint in our VPC and use mTLS between the private endpoint and Redwood runtime.
- Staging: happy to carve out a 2-week staging window the week of Jun 10–21.

Attached an updated network diagram (orbitworks_network_diagram_v2.pdf) with the TGW zones labeled. We're available for the proposed Wed 5/22 10:30–11:00 PDT slot.

-Ben
